title: Demotion gate — the rule that sends a live strategy back to paper

source.label: X1 project brief (verbatim): define a demotion gate

rows.rule: The strategy's mean closing line value over the trailing window turns non-positive with a one-sided t-test rejecting mean CLV > 0.
rows.threshold: mean CLV <= 0 and one-sided t p < 0.10
rows.why: CLV is the cleanest early evidence that the edge is gone: it moves before ROI does, and it is immune to the variance of final scores.

rows.rule: Peak-to-trough drawdown of the flat-stake signal bankroll breaches either absolute or relative limit.
rows.why: A drawdown larger than any plausible edge run is evidence the edge was never there — or is gone. The unit floor stops a young strategy being killed by noise.

rows.rule: Rolling hit rate falls below the break-even rate implied by the prices taken, with a one-sided binomial test.
rows.threshold: hit rate < break-even and one-sided binomial p < 0.10
rows.why: Catches a strategy that is still beating the close on tickets but losing them.

rows.rule: Any input behind a live signal fails its source check (unverified value, stale snapshot, broken feed), or a signal cannot be replayed from its recorded snapshot.
rows.why: An unverifiable live signal is an unmanaged bet. Suspend first, investigate second.
rows.action: immediate demotion to paper until the input passes its check again

rows.rule: A demoted strategy returns to live only by passing every promotion gate on NEW graded bets recorded after the demotion date. Pre-demotion data may not be reused, and D1-D3 must be clear on the new sample.
rows.threshold: >= 50 new graded bets, all promotion gates passed
rows.why: Without this rule a demotion is cosmetic: the same strategy would sail back on the same evidence that already failed.
rows.action: promotion re-considered; owner records the decision

cadence: Evaluated after every graded batch (at least weekly during the season).
authority: Demotion is automatic and logged; the owner may demote at any time for any reason, and may overrule an automatic demotion only by recording why in the decision register. Promotions are always a recorded decision.
uses: The signal block of the leaderboard split (data/leaderboard_split.json), never the staking block.
closes_question: Q-26 (the demotion rule was undefined and blocked gate G-13).

verification.note: These are policy definitions, not measurements: thresholds were set by design before any strategy is live (pre-registration), and every numeric value is reproduced here so it can be challenged before, not after, it binds.
